newsitem.title: UK: Launders quits Leeds after row with board.
newsitem.headline: Launders quits Leeds after row with board.

text.p: Leeds United chief executive Robin Launders resigned from the club on Monday over a rift with fellow directors of parent company Caspian Group Plc.

Caspian chairman Chris Akers said that Launders resigned after a board meeting on Monday morning. Akers said that there had been no boardroom split and that the loss of Launders should not alter the company's strategy.
Launders joined Leeds United last August, after a five-year stint as finance director of Manchester United Plc, Britain's largest listed soccer club.
He has received a pay-off from Caspian of some 150,000 stg -- equivalent to one year's salary.
Caspian acquired Leeds last year in a 16.5 million stg reverse takeover and plans to make the premier league club the centrepiece of a sports, media and leisure group.
Caspian shares slipped 2p to 26.5p on Monday.
